newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks close firmer, C-C Amatil surges.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks close firmer, C-C Amatil surges.

text.p: SPI Sycom 2,350.0 +4.0 US 30yr 7.07
10yrbond futs 91.890 +0.050 Gold NY 348.85 Lon fix 348.75
AUD cl US$0.7765 (Thurs $0.7815) CRB Index 241.62 -2.46
*Stocks close firmer, Coca-Cola Amatil heads gains, market looks to release of U.S. jobs data. Volume 278.44 million, value A$751.22 million, 1,067 stocks traded, 356 steady, 382 up, 329 down
Australian shares ended a touch firmer for a second day running despite a weaker U.S. market, led by a surging Coca-Cola Amatil in the wake of its A$3.4 billion Philippines soft drinks deal.
"It's not a bad performance and shows a bit of resilience, which we haven't seen for a while," said Austock Brokers research director David Perry.

The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended 8.5 points firmer at 2,369.5 in moderate trade after a 5.8 point rise on Thursday. The June share price futures contract was up 4.0 points at 2,350.0, a 19.5 point discount to the physical market.
Brokers said the market was aided by early short-covering in major stocks and some bargain hunting.

C-C Amatil rose A$1.40 on the day to close at A$14.20, and has now risen 18.8 percent since announcing its plan to acquire San Miguel Corp soft drink subsidiary Coca Cola Bottler Philippines Inc in exchange for equity.
The strong gains surprised some brokers following suggestions by analysts that the price paid was expensive, and that the Philippines plants could require high levels of capital expenditure.
There was also concern about the C-C Amatil's ability to deliver adequate profit growth, one broker said.
However, others said the jump had to be seen in the context of C-C Amatil's sharp fall from around A$18 late last year on earnings disappointments.
"A very good stock was really needing a bit of a blood transfusion and the market perceives that it's got that with this deal," said Intersuisse head of equities Andrew Sekely.

The release of domestic retail trade and building approvals data had little impact, but brokers said investors remained wary of the release of March U.S. payrolls, wages and unemployment data on Friday.
Analysts said figures showing a more robust than expected U.S. economy would add to fears among investors of a further hike in U.S. interest rates.
The Bank of Melbourne eased three cents to A$9.47 after comments by Treasurer Peter Costello and regulatory authorities were seen as negative for its takeover by Westpac Banking Corp.
Elsewhere, the Bank of Queensland, which is 45 percent owned by the state government, closed two cents higher at A$6.27 after reporting a first half profit down 22 percent at A$8.00 million.

Gold major Plutonic Resources bounced 24 cents to A$4.77, while shares in Foodland Associated were also stronger after the food retailer and wholesaler on Thursday reported a strong rise in its first half profit.
In other local markets, the Australian dollar fell to its lowest level since February after breaking through support. The Australian dollar was at US$0.7762 at 4.30 p.m. (0630 GMT).
Australian bond futures squeezed higher across the curve sparked by buying of the three-year bond contract.
